summary: In Greek mythology, Bias (Ancient Greek Βίας) is a Pylian warrior whom Nestor arrays with Pelagon, Alastor, Chromius, and Haemon when Poseidon rouses the Achaeans in Iliad 4 — Homer's "Bias, shepherd of the host." Distinct from Bias son of Amythaon, from the Athenian Bias under Menestheus, from the Trojan father of Laogonus, and from the Dulichian suitor.
etymology: Ancient Greek Βίας; Homeric epithet "shepherd of the host" (ποιμένα λαῶν) marks this Pylian officer in the catalogue of Nestor's captains.

sections.heading: Nestor's captain
paragraphs: In Iliad 4 Nestor the clear-voiced orator draws up his Pylians around mighty Pelagon, Alastor, Chromius, lord Haemon, and Bias, shepherd of the host — charioteers first with horses and cars, then the foot as a bulwark of battle. The poem gives this Bias no genealogy beyond that Pylian muster.
The atlas id bias-pylian is that Homeric Pylian alone.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: Not bias-aeolid (Amythaon's brother of Melampus and king of a third of Argos); not bias-athenian (valiant Bias with Menestheus at the ships); not bias-trojan (Priamid father of Laogonus and Dardanus); not bias-dulichium. All share Wikipedia's Bias (mythology) list.
